text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High egress error rate detected for VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d in eu-west-2. 18% of outbound connections failing (NAT gateway errors 502/504). Auto-escalation to sev2. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/vpc-egress
oncall-network: I'm oncall, investigating. Confirming scope — which subnets are failing?
opsbot: Metric spike: nat-gateway/egress-errors increased at 2026-03-15T02:12Z. Affected AZ: eu-west-2b. Instances showing SYN retransmits + conn resets.
sre-maria: I see increased conntrack table usage on nat-gateway-2 in eu-west-2b from CloudWatch. Possible conntrack leak from recent rollout of proxy service.
devops-aly: @sre-maria could this be the terraform NACL rule change rolled out last night? PR #1427 added an egress NACL deny for ephemeral ports in eu-west-2b for security audit.
sre-maria: Good call — checking terraform state now. If ephemeral ports are blocked that could break NAT translations and leave conntrack entries stuck.
eng-james: Customer-impact check: Support dashboard shows ~12 customers with degraded outbound calls to third-party APIs. No inbound app errors.
support-john: Confirmed: multiple support tickets citing 502s when calling payment provider between 02:10-02:20Z. Flagged customers with highest traffic.
oncall-network: Triage: Is service degradation across all AZs or just 2b? opsbot metrics show only eu-west-2b elevated errors.
incident-bot: Pager: On-call handoff to oncall-network at 2026-03-15T02:16Z. Incident channel created.
oncall-network: Plan: 1) Rollback recent NACL change in eu-west-2b
2) If rollback not immediate, add temporary NAT instance and update route table in affected private subnets
3) Mitigate conntrack by rotating NAT gateway (replace) if still unhealthy
Can we rollback TF quickly?
devops-aly: Rolling back PR #1427 now — applying a targeted change to NACLs in eu-west-2b. Patch apply in progress: `terraform apply -target=module.vpc.aws_network_acl_rule.ephemeral_block`
opsbot: Terraform apply started: apply id tf-7891. Streaming logs...
eng-james: While rollback runs, prepare NAT instance boot script. I'll spin a t3.medium NAT instance in the same subnet and add to route tables as emergency fallback.
eng-james: Boot script:
```
# boot-nat.sh
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
```
Will register IP and update private route tables to point 10.0.32.5 -> temporary NAT.
sre-maria: conntrack check (from NAT gateway logs): many TIME_WAIT -> established entries not clearing. conntrack count near 98% of limit. If rollback succeeds, entries should drain; if not, NAT needs replacement.
opsbot: Terraform apply succeeded in 18s: rule removal confirmed. NACL ephemeral deny removed for subnet-ids [subnet-aaa, subnet-bbb]
oncall-network: Rolling checks now. Can we confirm outbound succeeds from a canary instance in eu-west-2b?
eng-james: Running curl test from canary: `curl -v https://api.payment.example/health` -> initial 502, retry 200 after 30s.
support-john: Customer impact update: tickets showing recovery for ~8 of 12 affected customers. Notifying those customers proactively.
oncall-network: Keep NAT replacement on standby. If errors persist >5m, we'll detach and reattach NAT gateway or failover to temp NAT instance.
sre-maria: I triggered NAT gateway restart via control plane workaround (create new NAT gw and switch route table) — new nat-gw-zz created and associated to private RT in eu-west-2b.
opsbot: Route table update executed: rt-0x private subnets now target nat-gw-zz (change-id: rtchg-334)
eng-james: After route switch, canary curl returns 200 consistently for 3 min. CloudWatch egress errors trending down.
incident-bot: Severity reduced to sev3 at 2026-03-15T02:35Z. Notifying on-call and stakeholders.
oncall-network: Postmortem checklist: capture which terraform change caused it, confirm conntrack root cause, and recommend guardrails (TF plan checks, canary rollout of NACL changes). Also add traffic shaping to avoid conntrack exhaustion.
devops-aly: I'll open a rollback postmortem PR and tag infra-security for review. PR link: https://redwood/pull/1451
sre-maria: Metrics snapshot: peak conntrack 97%, dropped packets 14k, 502/504 spike lasted ~18 minutes. Affected AZ: eu-west-2b only. No data-plane leakage observed.
support-john: Customer comms: drafting incident banner and targeted emails for 12 customers — sending in 20m after signoff.
oncall-network: Any lingering risk? Need to audit other AZs for similar NACL rule drift.
eng-james: I'll add an automated ci check that rejects NACL rules that deny ephemeral ranges unless explicitly approved with mitigation steps.
incident-bot: Incident closed (initial mitigation complete) at 2026-03-15T03:05Z. Follow-up actions assigned to: devops-aly, sre-maria, eng-james, support-john. Runbook update scheduled.
support-john: Leaving notes for CS handoff: list of affected customer IDs, times, and mitigation performed. Will attach to postmortem.
opsbot: Created follow-up ticket TIC-2026-332: "NACL rollback and postmortem — eu-west-2b NAT conntrack" assigned to devops-aly.
sre-maria: Quick root-cause hypothesis for postmortem: NACL ephemeral deny prevented outbound port allocations causing NAT to maintain long-lived conntrack entries, combined with a proxy change that increased connection churn. Repro steps in follow-up.
oncall-network: Thanks all — great coordination. :clap:
support-john: I'll queue proactive outreach and keep open support tickets updated.
eng-james: I'll keep the temporary NAT instance on standby for 1 hour then decommission if stable.
incident-bot: Thread archived. Logs and transcript attached to TIC-2026-332.
